chapter: Idaho tours, Music Town and retirement
title: Retirement songwriting and the stalled Bicentennial project with Channel 13
summary: Spikes wrote religious songs and scripts such as The Biddy Mason Story, but could not get Channel 13 to respond about the Bicentennial.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well, after that, I went into the real estate business, and I stayed in that until '62, and then I retired, and I came home and I've written several songs and a lot of religious songs and "The Biddy Mason Story," "Stagecoach Mary," "Nightmare," "Three Passengers," and, oh, I don't know. I've got 'em around here. It... uh...but it seems like that I just couldn't find the right agent. I had agents, some of them I had a coupla years. They couldn't do nothing with it. I don't know, so I just got mad and called them all in and took it, and so, since [Mayor Tom] Bradley now--'course I knew him before he was in school, you see--and when this come out that they was going to do this BiCentennial [Los Angeles], I wrote to him and I told him that this ought to be used, and he say, "Yeah! That's a good idea." And he wrote Pisano and them a letter to use it, and he sent 'em over the stuff from his office, and they called me and told me they had it, and they turned it over to Channel 13, and they said, "We'll let you know," and they...and I've called a dozen times, and they won't even answer--[Marilyn] Solomon or [Marian] Morton. They... I've called them...some of them...for a week at a time, every other day, every day, and they say, "Well, she's busy. She's in...uh, counsel ...and she's not in her office..." That's the excuse I get. I leave my number but none of them has ever called.
Well, I think you ought to take it away from Channel 13 because I think now is the time to really do something with it.

Well, I had made up my mind that I was going to wait this week out but I don't have to wait for nobody because they haven't give me no...uh, any notice whether they gonna use it or they not gonna use it, and I even told them, I said, "Now, I've got addresses and things of people that were in business way back a hundred years ago that...that you probably could get commercials from. You know. And Ralphs' [a Southern California supermarket chain] there sent me a whole bunch of pictures a way back in the 1875 and '60...er, '80 down there, you know.
